title: SierpinskiCam: Camera-Controlled Video Retaking with Sierpinski Triangle Pattern Cues
claim: Even under large viewpoint changes with sparse source evidence, our conditioning yields faithful camera-following videos that preserve original scene content.
layout: 3 scene blocks stacked; source, trajectory, generated frames left-to-right; condition-video row
description: A gallery of three scenes stacked vertically, separated by a thin line: a red panda on a branch in a forest, a helmeted mouse beside a mousetrap, and an octopus on an underwater treasure chest. Each block starts at the left with three source-video frames, followed by a column of small 3D plots of camera trajectories drawn as frusta, shaded from blue (start) to red (end). To the right, under a header with an arrow reading Generated Video, are four columns of frames. The top scene also shows a condition video row, where a black-and-white Sierpinski triangle pattern fills the regions that the source does not cover. Generated rows show the scene viewed from new angles and positions. The eye goes first to the vivid photographic frames.
caption: SierpinskiCam for video retake generation. Given a source video and a target camera trajectory (blue →red), SierpinskiCam retakes the video under user-defined camera motions. Even under large viewpoint changes with sparse source evidence, our Sierpinski textured dome (top condition video) and negative rotary position embedding allow faithful following of the target camera trajectory while preserving the original scene content. Source videos are generated by Veo3 [7].
abstract: Generating novel renderings of a scene along user-defined camera trajectories from a single monocular video, dubbed video retaking, is a compelling but difficult problem in content creation and visual effects. Existing geometry-guided approaches reconstruct a 4D representation from the source video and render it along the target trajectory to condition video diffusion models. However, this guidance degrades as the target camera departs from the source trajectory, leaving newly revealed regions sparse or entirely missing. We propose SierpinskiCam, which addresses this limitation by augmenting geometry-based guidance with Sierpinski dome texture cues that contains rich trackable features even under large viewpoint changes. We further introduce a reference video conditioning mechanism that appends source-video tokens to the target-token sequence and separates the two streams with negative RoPE indices, enabling appearance grounding without architectural modification or per-video adaptation. Extensive experiments show that SierpinskiCam achieves significant gains in camera controllability, geometric consistency, and video quality across diverse and challenging retaking scenarios. Project page: https://hyelinnam.github.io/SierpinskiCam/.
